negative_findings.description: Every attempted WebFetch against www.nbrm.mk (register pages, bylaw index) returned HTTP 403 Forbidden, while the same pages are present in search-engine indexes.
negative_findings.result_summary: 3 of 3 nbrm.mk .nspx fetches returned 403; content confirmed to exist via search snippets. Treated as bot-defended-but-live, NOT dead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The single most important source family in this cell (statutory registers) cannot be collected with a naive HTTP client; the pipeline needs a headless browser or UA/header-tuned fetcher, otherwise this cell silently produces zero data.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated North Macedonian interchange-fee regulation (an MK analogue of EU Regulation 2015/751 IFR) was located, and no Commission for Protection of Competition (Комисија за заштита на конкуренцијата) decision on card interchange surfaced.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searched in mk and en for интерчејнџ / заменски надоместок / interchange cap. Only found that the PSPS Law defines 'заменски надоместок' (interchange fee); no cap-setting instrument identified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If no interchange cap exists, MK card economics differ structurally from the EU and any assumption of an EU-style 0.2%/0.3% cap would be wrong. This must be resolved from the statutory text before any market conclusion is drawn.

negative_findings.description: No official NBRSM page or document specifically dedicated to a domestic instant-payments scheme rulebook or go-live date was located; evidence for instant payments is currently indirect (media relaying NBRSM/ECB statements about joining a TIPS-based regional platform, plus SEPA accession).
negative_findings.result_summary: mk and en searches returned the MIPS RTGS page, media coverage, and EPC/EC SEPA material, but no primary instant-payments scheme documentation.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The go-live date and scheme rules are the key dated event for this cell; relying on media alone risks recording an announced date as an achieved one.

negative_findings.description: No machine-readable (API, CSV, open-data) endpoint was found for any NBRSM licence register; all evidence points to HTML pages and PDFs only.
negative_findings.result_summary: No data.gov.mk or NBRSM open-data endpoint surfaced for payment institution / EMI registers.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection must be scrape-and-diff rather than API polling, raising fragility and the need for change detection on page structure.

negative_findings.description: The exact Official Gazette citation of the PSPS Law is reported inconsistently across secondary sources (No. 90/22 appears in the ENER-derived summary; the seed prompt context suggested 178/21; the NBRSM consolidated-text filename carries suffix 144-25 implying a later amendment).
negative_findings.result_summary: Three different issue numbers encountered; none confirmed by direct reading of the Gazette.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The Gazette number and date are the anchor for every downstream regulatory event; the pipeline must resolve this from the consolidated PDF's own header rather than from search snippets.

negative_findings.description: Casys and KIBS (the domestic card processor and clearing house, likely 'оператори на платни системи' under the law) did not surface as licensed-operator entries in any accessible register listing during this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Targeted mk query naming Casys and KIBS returned only bank T&C PDFs and the NBRSM card-statistics page.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The payment system operator register is the pointer to domestic switch/clearing infrastructure; not confirming its contents leaves a hole in the actor map.

brief: North Macedonia's payments regulatory layer is centralised almost entirely in the National Bank (НБРСМ), which under the PSD2-transposing Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems (in force 1 January 2023) both writes the secondary legislation and maintains the three statutory public registers — payment institutions (with simplified-access PIs and agents), e-money institutions, and payment system operators — making nbrm.mk the single highest-value pointer in this cell. The practical obstacle is technical rather than legal: every nbrm.mk fetch returned HTTP 403, so the registers are live but bot-defended and require a headless-browser collector; the Ministry of Finance ENER consultation portal, the Official Gazette, and the Ministry's legal compendium serve as earlier-warning and non-blocked mirrors respectively. Externally, the EPC SEPA participant register and the European Commission's annual enlargement report give dated, independently verifiable milestones (SEPA geographical scope from 6 March 2025, operational readiness 5 October 2025) that cross-check domestic self-reporting, while the FIU's AML law supplies the cash-usage lever via the EUR 3,000 cash-payment ceiling. Two substantive holes remain: no domestic interchange-fee cap instrument could be located despite the law defining 'заменски надоместок', and instant-payments evidence is still media-level rather than primary scheme documentation.
